newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil- Firmer amid fewer Kuwaiti supplies.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil- Firmer amid fewer Kuwaiti supplies.

text.p: Singapore high sulphur fuel oil prices rose on firmer bids and reduced Kuwaiti exports, traders said on Wednesday.
A bid was seen for May 1-5 at $99.00 per tonne, $2.00 higher from Tuesday's bid at $97.00. While firm offers did not emerge, traders said there are still unsold supplies in the region.
Kuwait was heard to have sold a cargo of fuel oil at between $1.15 and $1.25 per barrel premium over Singapore spot quotes on a cost and freight basis to a trader.
Traders said Kuwait has only exported two cargoes of fuel oil for May, compared to four cargoes exported for April arrival.
They said domestic demand in Kuwait is expected to increase as the summer season begins, possibly dampening further exports.
A Mideast bunker trader was also heard offering supplies in Singapore amid a depressed bunker market in Fujiarah.
Traders said Iran is expected to export its usual four cargoes of fuel oil in May and some supplies were also heard from Bahrain.
Demand in Asia is projected to stay stagnant with China importing similar volumes in May as in April.
Hong Kong traders estimated China's May imports at 400,000 tonnes to 600,000 tonnes.
Bunker trade rose nearer the end of the trading day, taking away some length in the market.
In the fob Singapore market, the premium was discussed between 75 cents and 1.25 cents per tonne over spot quotes.
In the LSWR market, enquiries were thin but the recent KEPCO (Korean Electric Power Corp) purchase tender has provided some support.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
APR FUEL OIL SWAPS 98.25/98.75 96.50/97.50
MAY FUEL OIL SWAPS 97.75/98.50 96.25/97.25
*Dollars per barrel
